text:
erin: heads-up: a customer reported that setting a custom routing header from the console doesn't map to their quota. they set `X-Customer-Tier` but metrics show 'standard' bucket.
vik: do we have a request sample? could be case or aliasing issue.
luis: saw this yesterday in prod traces: edge lowercased header to `x-customer-tier` and an older matching rule only recognizes `X-Customer-Tier` exact-case.
erin: risky to change matching behavior globally without a rollout. proposal: add tolerant match (case-insensitive) behind a feature flag `header_case_tolerant` and ship lightweight SDK normalization to a canonical `x-rw-cust-tier`.
vik: SDKs: small change, non-breaking. python/go add normalizer util, TS add helper for fetch/axios. also add telemetry event `cust_tier_normalized`.
qa-bot: please add unit test for four cases: exact-case, all-lowercase, alias name, missing header fallback.
infra-sre: can roll flag as 2% canary this afternoon. we can monitor attribution delta.
luis: also check proxies that collapse multiple headers — ensure we merge not overwrite.
erin: timeline: today - SDK PRs + tests. canary tonight 02:00 UTC for 24h. if attribution delta < 0.5% we flip.
vik: i'll update console matcher code to accept either canonical or alias and to compare header names case-insensitively when flag is on.
infra-sre: deployed canary at 02:01 UTC. dashboards: https://console.redwood.run/dashboards/header-case-canary
qa-bot: smoke tests all green.
luis: initial telemetry shows ~700 normalized requests from various customers. no regressions so far.
erin: ok great. once SDK PRs merge we'll publish patch releases and post changelog.
vik: noted. adding migration note in quickstart and a sample snippet for each SDK.
erin: thanks everyone — looping back tomorrow with canary results.
